old: A Japanese 10 yen in bronze, dated Heisei 14 (2002), the fourteenth year of Emperor Akihito's reign. One side shows the Phoenix Hall of Byodoin temple in Uji, a thousand-year-old building so loved that it also appears on the 10,000 yen note. The other side frames a big 10 in a wreath of evergreen leaves. Japan has struck this design, nearly unchanged, since 1951, and it is still the 10 yen in everyday pockets today. The collection already holds two Showa-era strikes of the same design from 1982 and 1988; this is its first Heisei one.
